thung-phra.name: Thung Phra Pho Park
thung-phra.lead: A single object tells the story of a port town

then.headline: From a riverside field to a town park
then.body: Accessible documents have not verified the exact founding year, creator, or initial project of Thung Phra Pho Park. Thus, the "origin of the park" can only be told as far as evidence allows. The park should not be directly linked to the tin mining era or maritime trade because there is no confirmed continuity. The context of the area is Takua Pa old town, which has a history of settlement and trade across various eras, including the Chinese community and tin economy. However, the confirmed role of Thung Phra Pho in contemporary documents is a public open space for town activities, not a mining building or an archaeological site with a clear founder.

before.headline: A public space handling water, merit making, and town adaptation
before.body: In 2013 (2556 BE), the park was named in the building control announcement for the Takua Pa old town area, meaning it is within the old town landscape where the state regulates construction. However, the announcement did not state the founding year or original form of the park. The municipality's action plan for the 2022 fiscal year indicated a project to install an electrical control cabinet in the park with a budget of 460,000 baht, as well as a project to dredge the Thung Phra Pho canal and build a Takua Pa canal pier (Thung Phra Pho). This reflects that the park is related to the town's water management and infrastructure. Meanwhile, news from 2013 noted that Thung Phra Pho was a site for installing water pumps during floods. Old town project documents state that the Loy Krathong festival is held here on the full moon day of the 12th lunar month, featuring krathong contests, performances, and local games. Found evidence has not verified any direct impact from the 2004 tsunami, abandonment, change of hands, or specific registration as a historical site for the park.

now.headline: A municipal park that remains a stage for daily life
now.body: Current map data identifies Thung Phra Pho as a public park in the Talat Yai subdistrict, near Wat Na Muang (a local temple), Fire Station 2, and the old town wall. It still serves as an open space in the old town, but no official announcement has verified the opening hours, admission fee, or specific facilities. A confirmed use in 2026 was the Takuapa Walk Rally organised by Takua Pa Khiri Khet School on 8 March 2026 at Thung Phra Pho Park and the old town area, reflecting its use as an outdoor learning space, health promotion site, and venue for local culture. Municipal documents also confirm its use for health and children, such as a health park and playground, while old town documents note Loy Krathong as an annual activity. However, recent physical condition reports, long-term restoration projects, or specific caretakers beyond the municipality have not been verified.

riverwalk.name: Takuapa Riverwalk
riverwalk.lead: Observing town life through food and the river

then.headline: From a mining town port to a riverside market space
then.body: Available evidence describes the history of the Takua Pa town area and the pier, rather than specifying the exact origin of this riverside market. Takua Pa has been a port town and a centre for goods exchange since ancient times, before growing from tin mining and water trade. The old town is situated in a location surrounded by rivers on three sides, making it suitable for navigation, trade, and town defence.

before.headline: When mining slowed, the pier became a memory and was then revived
before.body: In the later period, the area was revitalised in the form of a community market under the name "Takuapa Riverwalk Ruamjai Pracharat". A Department of Internal Trade document with data as of 31 January 2019 (2562 BE) specified its location next to Wat Yan Yao (a local temple) and opening hours on Saturdays from 15:00 to 20:00. Evidence has not verified if the market was directly impacted by the 2004 tsunami or registered as a historical site under the market's name.

now.headline: A Saturday canal side market that brings old town memories back to life
now.body: The market is located in the old town landscape featuring Chinese and Sino-Portuguese buildings. Riverside activities by the municipality still appear in planning documents, such as almsgiving along the river next to Wat Nikornwararam (Wat Yan Yao), and the Ministry of Culture lists a seafood festival specifying the market as the venue. However, the name of the agency or person directly managing the market has not been verified, nor have permanent restoration projects for the market itself in 2026.

highlights.title: Local food and snacks
highlights.detail: Stalls selling local sweets, native food, OTOP products, and Takua Pa's specialities.

highlights.title: Canal side atmosphere
highlights.detail: The market is located along the Takua Pa canal or river, suitable for river viewing and photography.

highlights.title: Performances and music
highlights.detail: User reviews indicate there is live music by students at times.

highlights.title: Connecting to the old town
highlights.detail: Located near Takua Pa old town and the Sino-Portuguese buildings of the Talat Yai community.

getting_there.text: Travel to the riverside area or Sri Takuapa Road near Wat Yan Yao. Sources suggest using local hired vehicles or motorcycle taxis from the Takua Pa bus terminal.

did_you_know: The term "Chap Se" used for the old commercial district is related to a Hokkien Chinese word and the old Takua Pa pier.
Takua Pa old town has evidence of water trade with merchant ships from China and Myanmar.

culture-street.name: Takua Pa Old Town Cultural Street
culture-street.lead: Reading windows, shop signs, and life on the street

then.headline: From a mining town commercial street to a stage for past stories
then.body: This street was not originally built as a tourist attraction, but grew within Takua Pa old town, which was a port town and water trade centre before reaching its peak during the tin mining era. Chinese people from the mainland, Penang, and Singapore came to trade and mine, leading to rows of shophouses, shops, hotels, coffee shops, and service businesses along Udomthara Road and Sri Takuapa Road. The buildings on both sides are therefore evidence of a multicultural town, featuring both Chinese style and colonial influenced shophouses linked to the Baba community. The street served as the town's commercial and residential axis, not a walking street like today. When the walking street project began in 2007 (2550 BE) through a collaboration between the TAT Phang Nga Office, Takua Pa Town Municipality, Talat Yai community, and Senanuchrangsan community, the original street was used as a public space to tell past stories and revive the community economy under the name "Takua Pa Old Town, Telling Stories of the Past".

before.headline: The mining town slowed down, but the old street did not disappear
before.body: After the mining companies closed and tin ore declined, the old commercial district economy slowed down. Some buildings remained in good condition, while others deteriorated over time. Area studies point out that organising the cultural street utilised stories, food, local wisdom, and original architecture as capital to bring people and income back to the district. The project name later changed from "Takua Pa Old Town, Telling Stories of the Past" to "Takua Pa Old Town Cultural Street". The Department of Internal Trade's market registry states the founding or promotion date as 17 December 2017, but news sources indicate activities began in 2007. Thus, it is suggested, not settled, that these are two different milestones: the start of activities and the registration or market promotion point. In 2022, the province and local bodies still organised activities during the green season with free Pho Thong (local bus) rides, showing the street was used as a tool to distribute income and draw people back to the old district. No specific evidence was found that the entire street was damaged by the 2004 tsunami or registered as a historical site in its entirety.

now.headline: A Sunday market that keeps the old town alive
now.body: The Department of Internal Trade's market registry notes that the Takua Pa Old Town Cultural Street is located on Sri Takuapa and Udomthara Roads, opening on Sundays from 14:00 to 20:00 with free entry to activities. This data specifies caretakers at the market system level but does not name a separate legal entity responsible for the street. Today, the street still functions as a market and community learning space, featuring local food and snacks, basketry, crafts, performances, Baba attire, photo exhibitions, and street art. The old Sino-Portuguese buildings remain the main backdrop for activities, with conditions ranging from well conserved to showing signs of wear over time. However, no major restoration project announcement specifically for this street was found in checked sources. Past news confirms the continuous holding of events at least in 2022 and community activities on the street in 2024, concluding that the street is still active as a cultural market and local activity space, though actual opening hours may change by season or organiser announcements.

iron-bridge.name: Boon Soong Iron Bridge
iron-bridge.lead: Looking at the steel frame and recalling the miners' journey

then.headline: From a tin dredger to a workers' bridge
then.body: The story of the bridge began in Takua Pa during the tin mining era, when the Boon Soong tin dredging company was located on the opposite side of the old market. The Takua Pa canal, over 40 metres wide, made it necessary for workers and villagers to row boats back and forth, which was especially difficult during floods. The local database of Prince of Songkla University notes that Mr Chuti Boon Soong, a mining entrepreneur, initially initiated a wooden bridge for walking and cycling. Later, in 1968 (2511 BE), steel from a decommissioned tin dredger was assembled into the Khok Khanoon iron bridge, over 200 metres long, crossing the Takua Pa river. The bridge was not merely an industrial structure, but a shortcut for labour, a route for transporting goods, and a daily connection between the old market and the mining area of a town driven by tin. Verifiable evidence confirms the role of mining and commuting, but contemporary documents linking the bridge directly to maritime trade, Hokkien Chinese people, or the governor system have not been found.

before.headline: When the mines went quiet, the bridge became a mining town trace
before.body: When the mining business ceased, the bridge did not disappear with the ore dredger, but changed its role from a working structure to a community transit route and evidence of the industrial landscape. The ONEP database states that the old ore dredger in its original condition can still be seen from the bridge area, while contemporary travel sources call this bridge a symbol of Takua Pa's mining past. In later periods, the bridge was told and presented as a tourist attraction and photo spot, and also appeared as a location in the film Wonderful Town (2007) according to location tracking articles. However, this review has not verified the exact year the mine closed, the year of major restorations, direct impacts from the 2004 tsunami, or registration as a historical site by the Fine Arts Department, so these events should not be added as facts.

now.headline: A mining heritage that remains a passageway and destination
now.body: Today, the Boon Soong Iron Bridge still functions as a community transit route, with field data and reviews stating that villagers use it for walking and riding motorcycles across. At the same time, Takua Pa Town Municipality categorises it as a tourist attraction, and TAT travel sources feature current photos of the site. The bridge thus sits halfway between a practical structure and a landmark where people come to enjoy the view and take photos. The latest evidence found is NBT news on 30 January 2026, which introduced the bridge as a mining heritage intertwined with Takua Pa and noted it was temporarily closed to accommodate a foreign film shoot. Additionally, municipal budget documents found include items related to the maintenance and improvement of the bridge entrance area, but documents verifying direct structural restoration projects have not been found. Opening hours, admission fees, specific event caretakers, and the latest safety conditions must therefore be verified on site.

highlights.title: Steel structure about 200 metres long
highlights.detail: The bridge spans the Takua Pa river and connects the main road area with the old ore dredger site.

highlights.title: Traces of the mining industry
highlights.detail: Built with steel from a decommissioned tin dredger, and the old dredger can be seen at the end of the bridge.

highlights.title: Fields and mountain views
highlights.detail: From the bridge, green fields, trees, and mountain ranges are visible, making it suitable for sightseeing and photography.

highlights.title: Community transit route
highlights.detail: The bridge is still a route used by villagers, so one should be careful of vehicles while visiting.

getting_there.text: Travel along Rat Bamrung Road towards Takua Pa old town; the bridge is on the left, about 2 kilometres from the town centre.

did_you_know: The iron bridge structure was built using steel from a decommissioned tin dredger, not new steel produced specifically for the bridge.
Before the iron bridge, workers and villagers had to use rowboats to cross the canal, and there used to be a wooden bridge for walking and cycling.
The bridge appeared in a location tracking article for the film Wonderful Town (2007).
